The OTIF score that hid the real problem

A headline OTIF score can remain stable while customer promises change repeatedly and the internal measure stops before confirmed delivery.

By Pupsi Phull2 minute read

Evidence boundary. Published metrics retain their stated source and context. Diagrams are illustrative and contain no client data.

Challenge

OTIF is useful. It is not the same thing as customer experience. The measure can look healthy while orders still need manual intervention and the customer waits for a promise that has moved more than once.

Diagnosis

Reconstruct requirement, commitment, promise change, despatch, delivery confirmation and exception handling as one event sequence. Then test which date and event the organisation uses as success.

Rebuild

Agree a service definition, preserve the original and changed promises, show exceptions before failure and assign ownership for each decision point.

Questions for the reader

  • Does the measure stop at despatch or confirmed delivery?
  • How many promise changes occur before a line scores on time?
  • Which exceptions were imported and which were created internally?
  • What management effort is invisible in the score?
